label: script
not_in_script: normal appetite, no breathlessness or chest pain, no thoughts of self-harm, a clear chest and a normal body mass index: from the script's marking scheme, not from its conversation
the reasons of the investigations: one line each, in the script's own sense

scenario.reasoning: Three months of tiredness in a woman of 34 with poor sleep, a heavy workload, a great deal of coffee, heavy periods and a mother with thyroid disease, and nothing sinister. There is no single diagnosis to reach: the right answer is a broad list and a sensible set of blood tests. A learner is most likely to settle on one label, such as thyroid or low mood.

patient.name: Ms Charlotte Hughes
patient.manner: Friendly and open, tired, a little worried that it is all in her head.

scenario.opening_words: Morning, doctor. Honestly, I'm just exhausted all the time. I thought I should get checked, maybe get some bloods done. I don't know what's wrong with me.

facts.fact: It has been a few months now, maybe three. It crept up. I wake up and I already feel like I need to go back to bed.
I sleep, but I never feel I have actually rested. I am probably on my phone too late, work emails and then scrolling. I get maybe six hours.
Work is full on. We had a restructure and I am covering two roles. I am coping, but I am running on coffee.
I drink four or five cups of coffee a day, more on a bad day.
My mood is a bit flat, not depressed exactly. I still enjoy things when I get to them. I have not been to the gym in weeks.
My focus on my work is fine. It just takes more out of me than it used to.
My weight is about the same.
I have had no night sweats and no fevers.
I have found no lumps, and my bowels are normal.
My periods are regular but on the heavier side. They always have been.
I am no more thirsty than normal and I do not pass urine more than normal.
I have a couple of glasses of wine at the weekend and nothing in the week.
My mum is on thyroid tablets, I think for an underactive thyroid.
I have no breathlessness and no chest pain.
I have no thoughts of harming myself.

scenario.ideas: I do not know what is wrong with me.
scenario.concerns: I have wondered whether it is just in my head.
scenario.expectations: I thought I should get checked, and maybe have some blood tests.

investigations.reason: To rule out a sugar problem.

plan.step: Advice on sleep: the phone out of the bedroom
Cut the coffee from five cups to two, before midday
Review with the results in about two weeks
Keep an eye on her mood, with a questionnaire if anything more develops

scenario.safety_net: If she starts losing weight without trying, has drenching night sweats, finds a lump or becomes breathless, she comes back sooner and does not wait for the appointment.

data_gathering: Ask about weight loss, night sweats, fevers and lumps.
Ask about thyroid disease, anaemia, diabetes or coeliac disease in the family.
Examine: pulse, blood pressure, the neck and the abdomen.
management: Keep the differential broad and name no single cause.
Send a baseline set of blood tests: blood count and ferritin, thyroid, HbA1c, kidney and liver, a coeliac screen, vitamin D and CRP.
Advise on sleep and on coffee.
Review with the results in about two weeks.
Tell her what should bring her back sooner.
relating: Find out that she wonders whether it is all in her head, and answer it.
Say honestly that there is no single label today.
